docs.title: langchain-openapi
docs.text:
Convert OpenAPI specifications into native, production-grade LangChain tools for AI agents.

langchain_openapi automatically parses OpenAPI v3.0 and v3.1 specifications and generates dynamic, strongly typed LangChain StructuredTools. No code generation or manual tool writing is required.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• ⚡ Zero-Code Tool Generation: Instant runtime conversion from OpenAPI JSON/YAML to LangChain tools.
  • 🔒 Comprehensive Authentication: Built-in support for Bearer Tokens, API Keys, Basic Auth, Cookies, and custom request providers.
  • 🛡️ Production Middleware Pipeline: Onion-style request/response interceptors for retries, rate-limiting, caching, logging, and result pagination.
  • 🎯 Type-Safe Validation: Dynamic Pydantic schema generation ensures LLM inputs are validated before HTTP execution.
  • 🌐 Async & Sync Support: Fully asynchronous execution engine powered by httpx.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from langchain_openapi import OpenAPIToolkit

# Load spec from remote URL or local file
toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url("https://api.crossref.org/swagger-docs")

# Get dynamically generated LangChain tools
tools = toolkit.get_tools()

print(f"Generated {len(tools)} tools:")
for tool in tools:
    print(f"- {tool.name}: {tool.description}")

docs.title: Architecture & Core Pipeline
docs.text: langchain-openapi processes raw OpenAPI specs into native LangChain tools using a clean, modular pipeline.

docs.title: Execution Pipeline
docs.text:
OpenAPI Spec (JSON / YAML / Dict)
              │
              ▼
       OpenAPILoader
              │
              ▼
        OpenAPIParser
              │
              ▼
      SchemaConverter ────► Pydantic Dynamic Models
              │
              ▼
    LangChainToolFactory
              │
              ▼
      AsyncHTTPExecutor
              │
              ▼
     Middleware Pipeline (Retry, Cache, RateLimit, Logging, Pagination)
              │
              ▼
      Request Providers (Authentication & Header Mutations)
              │
              ▼
         httpx.AsyncClient (Target HTTP API)

docs.title: 1. OpenAPILoader
docs.text: In-gests raw JSON/YAML specifications from local disk files, remote HTTP endpoints, or in-memory dictionaries. Normalizes encoding and format.

docs.title: 2. OpenAPIParser
docs.text: Translates raw specification dictionaries into strongly-typed internal data models (Operation, Parameter, RequestBody, Response, Schema). Resolves internal $ref pointers using ReferenceResolver.

docs.title: 3. SchemaConverter & PydanticFactory
docs.text: Converts JSON Schema representations into dynamic Pydantic models at runtime using pydantic.create_model(). Ensures incoming LLM function call arguments adhere to strict type schemas.

docs.title: 4. LangChainToolFactory
docs.text: Translates parsed Operation models into executable LangChain StructuredTool instances.

docs.title: 5. AsyncHTTPExecutor
docs.text: Orchestrates request building, middleware execution, provider transformations, and asynchronous network transport.

docs.title: 6. Middleware Pipeline
docs.text: Intercepts outgoing requests and incoming responses to apply retries, rate limiting, caching, result aggregation, and sanitized telemetry.

docs.title: 7. Request Providers
docs.text: Applies authentication schemes (Bearer tokens, API Keys, Basic Auth) and static headers before network transport.

docs.title: Authentication & Request Providers
docs.text: langchain-openapi uses a pluggable RequestProvider interface to handle authentication and arbitrary request mutations before requests are sent to target APIs.

docs.title: 1. Bearer Auth Provider
docs.text:
Injects an Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN> header.

from langchain_openapi import BearerAuthProvider, OpenAPIToolkit

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.github.com/openapi",
    provider=BearerAuthProvider(token="ghp_secret_token"),
)

docs.title: 2. API Key Header Provider
docs.text:
Injects an API key in a designated request header.

from langchain_openapi import APIKeyHeaderProvider, OpenAPIToolkit

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    provider=APIKeyHeaderProvider(key="secret_key_123", header="X-API-Key"),
)

docs.title: 3. API Key Query Provider
docs.text:
Appends an API key as a query parameter.

from langchain_openapi import APIKeyQueryProvider, OpenAPIToolkit

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    provider=APIKeyQueryProvider(key="secret_key_123", parameter="api_key"),
)

docs.title: 4. Basic Auth Provider
docs.text:
Injects HTTP Basic Authentication credentials.

from langchain_openapi import BasicAuthProvider, OpenAPIToolkit

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    provider=BasicAuthProvider(username="admin", password="password123"),
)

docs.title: Combining Providers with CompositeProvider
docs.text:
Chain multiple request providers sequentially using CompositeProvider:

from langchain_openapi import (
    BearerAuthProvider,
    CompositeProvider,
    CookiesProvider,
    OpenAPIToolkit,
    StaticHeadersProvider,
)

composite = CompositeProvider(
    [
        BearerAuthProvider(token="jwt_token_here"),
        StaticHeadersProvider({"User-Agent": "langchain-openapi/1.0"}),
        CookiesProvider({"session_id": "sess_999"}),
    ]
)

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    provider=composite,
)

docs.title: Production Middleware Pipeline
docs.text: langchain_openapi provides an onion-style middleware architecture for cross-cutting production concerns.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Middleware components wrap the HTTP execution engine in sequential order:

Request ──► Middleware 1 ──► Middleware 2 ──► Transport Call ──► API
                                                                  │
Response ◄── Middleware 1 ◄── Middleware 2 ◄──────────────────────┘

docs.title: 1. Retry Middleware
docs.text:
Handles network transport exceptions and transient HTTP error status codes (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) with configurable backoff strategies.

from langchain_openapi import OpenAPIToolkit, RetryMiddleware

retry_mw = RetryMiddleware(
    retries=3,
    backoff="exponential",  # or "fixed"
    backoff_factor=0.5,
    retry_status_codes=(429, 500, 502, 503, 504),
)

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    middleware=[retry_mw],
)

docs.title: 2. Rate Limit Middleware
docs.text:
Enforces global request rate limits across all tools using a token bucket algorithm.

from langchain_openapi import OpenAPIToolkit, RateLimitMiddleware

rate_mw = RateLimitMiddleware(requests_per_second=10.0)

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    middleware=[rate_mw],
)

docs.title: 3. Cache Middleware
docs.text:
Caches GET response payloads with TTL expiration.

from langchain_openapi import CacheMiddleware, InMemoryCacheBackend, OpenAPIToolkit

cache_mw = CacheMiddleware(
    ttl=300.0,
    backend=InMemoryCacheBackend(),
    cache_authenticated=False,
)

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    middleware=[cache_mw],
)

docs.title: 4. Pagination Middleware
docs.text:
Automatically aggregates multi-page API responses when a tool is invoked with __paginate__=True.

from langchain_openapi import OpenAPIToolkit, PaginationMiddleware

pag_mw = PaginationMiddleware(max_pages=5, max_items=500)

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    middleware=[pag_mw],
)

# Tool execution with pagination enabled
# await tool.ainvoke({"query": "search_term", "__paginate__": True})

docs.title: 5. Logging Middleware
docs.text:
Logs outgoing request URLs and incoming response status codes with automatic sensitive header/credential redaction.

from langchain_openapi import LoggingMiddleware, OpenAPIToolkit

log_mw = LoggingMiddleware()

toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/spec.json",
    middleware=[log_mw],
)

docs.title: 3. Invoke a Tool Directly

    tool = toolkit.get_tool("search_works")
    result = await tool.ainvoke({"query": "LangGraph"})
    print(result)


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Tool Filtering & Selection
docs.text:
Filter generated tools by HTTP methods, tags, or operation names:

# Filter by HTTP Method
read_only_toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/openapi.json",
    methods=["GET"],
)

# Filter by Tags
user_toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/openapi.json",
    tags=["Users", "Profiles"],
)

# Include specific operation names
included_toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/openapi.json",
    include=["get_user_by_id", "list_users"],
)

# Exclude specific operation names
excluded_toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
    "https://api.example.com/openapi.json",
    exclude=["delete_user_by_id"],
)

class AsyncHTTPExecutor:
    """Generic asynchronous HTTP executor for executing OpenAPI operations.

    The executor is completely decoupled from AI agents and LangChain interfaces.

    Attributes:
        base_url: Optional default base URL for API endpoints.
        client: Optional injected httpx.AsyncClient instance.
        provider: RequestProvider instance for authentication and mutation.
        pipeline: MiddlewarePipeline for processing request/response lifecycle.
        timeout: Execution timeout in seconds.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
        provider: RequestProvider | None = None,
        auth: AuthProvider | None = None,
        middleware: Sequence[Middleware] | None = None,
        timeout: float = 30.0,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize AsyncHTTPExecutor.

        Args:
            base_url: Optional base URL prefix for operations.
            client: Optional httpx.AsyncClient for dependency injection.
            provider: RequestProvider instance for request mutation & authentication.
            auth: Legacy AuthProvider instance for backwards compatibility.
            middleware: Sequence of Middleware objects to process HTTP requests.
            timeout: Request timeout duration in seconds (default 30.0s).
        """
        self.base_url = base_url
        self._client = client

        if provider is not None:
            self.provider = provider
        elif auth is not None:
            self.provider = AuthProviderAdapter(auth)
        else:
            self.provider = NoAuthProvider()

        self.pipeline = MiddlewarePipeline(middleware)
        self.timeout = timeout
        self._builder = RequestBuilder(base_url=base_url)
        self._parser = ResponseParser()

    async def execute(
        self,
        operation: Operation,
        arguments: dict[str, Any],
        base_url_override: str | None = None,
    ) -> ResponseData:
        """Execute an OpenAPI Operation with the supplied arguments.

        Args:
            operation: Target Operation model.
            arguments: Input arguments dictionary.
            base_url_override: Optional base URL override.

        Returns:
            Normalized ResponseData object containing status, headers, and parsed body.

        Raises:
            RequestValidationError: If path parameters are missing.
            AuthenticationError: If authentication configuration fails.
            ProviderError: If a request provider fails.
            ExecutionTimeoutError: If request execution times out.
            HTTPExecutionError: If network or transport error occurs.
            ResponseParsingError: If response parsing fails.
        """
        # 1. Build HTTP request metadata
        built_req = self._builder.build(
            operation=operation,
            arguments=arguments,
            base_url_override=base_url_override,
        )

        start_time = time.monotonic()

        # 2. Perform network request using client or dedicated context
        try:
            if self._client is not None:
                response = await self._send_request(self._client, built_req)
            else:
                async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self.timeout) as client:
                    response = await self._send_request(client, built_req)
        except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
            logger.error(
                "Request timed out for %s after %.1fs",
                sanitize_request_log(built_req.method, built_req.url),
                self.timeout,
            )
            raise ExecutionTimeoutError(
                f"HTTP request to '{built_req.url}' timed out after {self.timeout}s."
            ) from exc
        except (
            RequestValidationError,
            AuthenticationError,
            ProviderError,
            ResponseParsingError,
        ):
            raise
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            logger.error(
                "HTTP execution failed for %s: %s",
                sanitize_request_log(built_req.method, built_req.url),
                exc,
            )
            raise HTTPExecutionError(
                f"HTTP request execution failed for '{built_req.url}': {exc}"
            ) from exc

        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
        logger.info(
            "Executed HTTP %s -> Status %d (%.3fs)",
            sanitize_request_log(built_req.method, built_req.url),
            response.status_code,
            elapsed,
        )

        # 3. Parse and return normalized response
        return self._parser.parse(response)

    async def _send_request(
        self, client: httpx.AsyncClient, req_data: Any
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "method": req_data.method,
            "url": req_data.url,
            "headers": req_data.headers,
            "params": req_data.params,
            "json": req_data.json_body,
            "timeout": self.timeout,
        }

        request = client.build_request(**kwargs)

        # Apply cookies if present on BuiltRequest
        if req_data.cookies:
            cookie_hdr = "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in req_data.cookies.items())
            request.headers["Cookie"] = cookie_hdr

        # Apply request provider mutations (auth, headers, cookies, etc.)
        request = await self.provider.apply(request)

        # Execute request through middleware pipeline down to transport
        async def transport_call(req: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
            return await client.send(req)

        return await self.pipeline.execute(request, transport_call)

class RequestBuilder:
    """Builder for translating Operation models into BuiltRequest instances."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize RequestBuilder.

        Args:
            base_url: Default base URL for API requests.
        """
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/") if base_url else ""

    def build(
        self,
        operation: Operation,
        arguments: dict[str, Any],
        base_url_override: str | None = None,
    ) -> BuiltRequest:
        """Build an HTTP request representation for an operation and arguments.

        Args:
            operation: Internal Operation model.
            arguments: Input arguments dictionary.
            base_url_override: Optional base URL override.

        Returns:
            A BuiltRequest object containing request parameters and payload.

        Raises:
            RequestValidationError: If a required path parameter is missing.
        """
        method = operation.method.value.upper()
        base_url = base_url_override.rstrip("/") if base_url_override else self.base_url

        path_template = operation.path
        query_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
        headers: dict[str, str] = {}
        cookies: dict[str, str] = {}
        consumed_args: set[str] = set()

        # Handle special paginate/__paginate__ argument for pagination middleware
        if arguments.get("paginate") or arguments.get("__paginate__"):
            headers["X-LangChain-Paginate"] = "true"
            consumed_args.add("paginate")
            consumed_args.add("__paginate__")

        # 1. Process operation parameters
        for param in operation.parameters:
            name = param.name
            val = arguments.get(name)

            if param.location == ParameterLocation.PATH:
                if val is None:
                    raise RequestValidationError(
                        f"Missing required path parameter '{name}' "
                        f"for operation '{operation.name}'."
                    )
                placeholder = f"{{{name}}}"
                path_template = path_template.replace(placeholder, str(val))
                consumed_args.add(name)

            elif param.location == ParameterLocation.QUERY:
                if val is not None:
                    query_params[name] = val
                    consumed_args.add(name)

            elif param.location == ParameterLocation.HEADER:
                if val is not None:
                    headers[name] = str(val)
                    consumed_args.add(name)

            elif param.location == ParameterLocation.COOKIE:
                if val is not None:
                    cookies[name] = str(val)
                    consumed_args.add(name)

        # 2. Construct final URL
        if base_url:
            full_url = f"{base_url}/{path_template.lstrip('/')}"
        else:
            full_url = path_template

        # 3. Process Request Body
        json_body: Any = None
        if operation.request_body:
            if "body" in arguments:
                json_body = arguments["body"]
            else:
                unconsumed = {
                    k: v for k, v in arguments.items() if k not in consumed_args
                }
                if unconsumed:
                    json_body = unconsumed

            if json_body is not None and "Content-Type" not in headers:
                headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

        return BuiltRequest(
            method=method,
            url=full_url,
            headers=headers,
            params=query_params,
            json_body=json_body,
            cookies=cookies,
        )

def build(
    self,
    operation: Operation,
    arguments: dict[str, Any],
    base_url_override: str | None = None,
) -> BuiltRequest:
    """Build an HTTP request representation for an operation and arguments.

    Args:
        operation: Internal Operation model.
        arguments: Input arguments dictionary.
        base_url_override: Optional base URL override.

    Returns:
        A BuiltRequest object containing request parameters and payload.

    Raises:
        RequestValidationError: If a required path parameter is missing.
    """
    method = operation.method.value.upper()
    base_url = base_url_override.rstrip("/") if base_url_override else self.base_url

    path_template = operation.path
    query_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
    headers: dict[str, str] = {}
    cookies: dict[str, str] = {}
    consumed_args: set[str] = set()

    # Handle special paginate/__paginate__ argument for pagination middleware
    if arguments.get("paginate") or arguments.get("__paginate__"):
        headers["X-LangChain-Paginate"] = "true"
        consumed_args.add("paginate")
        consumed_args.add("__paginate__")

    # 1. Process operation parameters
    for param in operation.parameters:
        name = param.name
        val = arguments.get(name)

        if param.location == ParameterLocation.PATH:
            if val is None:
                raise RequestValidationError(
                    f"Missing required path parameter '{name}' "
                    f"for operation '{operation.name}'."
                )
            placeholder = f"{{{name}}}"
            path_template = path_template.replace(placeholder, str(val))
            consumed_args.add(name)

        elif param.location == ParameterLocation.QUERY:
            if val is not None:
                query_params[name] = val
                consumed_args.add(name)

        elif param.location == ParameterLocation.HEADER:
            if val is not None:
                headers[name] = str(val)
                consumed_args.add(name)

        elif param.location == ParameterLocation.COOKIE:
            if val is not None:
                cookies[name] = str(val)
                consumed_args.add(name)

    # 2. Construct final URL
    if base_url:
        full_url = f"{base_url}/{path_template.lstrip('/')}"
    else:
        full_url = path_template

    # 3. Process Request Body
    json_body: Any = None
    if operation.request_body:
        if "body" in arguments:
            json_body = arguments["body"]
        else:
            unconsumed = {
                k: v for k, v in arguments.items() if k not in consumed_args
            }
            if unconsumed:
                json_body = unconsumed

        if json_body is not None and "Content-Type" not in headers:
            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

    return BuiltRequest(
        method=method,
        url=full_url,
        headers=headers,
        params=query_params,
        json_body=json_body,
        cookies=cookies,
    )

class ResponseParser:
    """Parser for attempting JSON decoding and standardizing HTTP responses."""

    def parse(self, response: httpx.Response) -> ResponseData:
        """Parse an httpx.Response into a normalized ResponseData object.

        Args:
            response: The raw httpx.Response instance.

        Returns:
            A ResponseData object containing status, headers, and parsed body.

        Raises:
            ResponseParsingError: If reading response content fails.
        """
        try:
            status_code = response.status_code
            headers = dict(response.headers)

            # Attempt JSON decoding if response content exists
            if response.content:
                try:
                    body: Any = response.json()
                    logger.debug("Successfully decoded response body as JSON")
                except Exception:
                    body = response.text
                    logger.debug("Response is not JSON, decoded as plain text")
            else:
                body = None

            return ResponseData(
                status_code=status_code,
                headers=headers,
                body=body,
                raw=response,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to parse response: %s", exc)
            raise ResponseParsingError(
                f"Catastrophic error parsing HTTP response: {exc}"
            ) from exc

class OpenAPILoader:
    """Loader for obtaining normalized OpenAPI specifications from various sources.

    Supported sources include local JSON/YAML files, remote URLs, and in-memory dicts.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        load_fn: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]],
        source_info: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize loader with a fetch callable and a source description string.

        Args:
            load_fn: A zero-argument callable that returns a raw spec dictionary.
            source_info: Human-readable description of the source for logging.
        """
        self._load_fn = load_fn
        self._source_info = source_info

    @classmethod
    def from_url(
        cls,
        url: str,
        timeout: float = 30.0,
        headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> "OpenAPILoader":
        """Create an OpenAPILoader for a remote URL source.

        Args:
            url: HTTP or HTTPS URL of the OpenAPI specification.
            timeout: Request timeout in seconds (default: 30.0).
            headers: Optional dictionary of HTTP headers for the request.

        Returns:
            An OpenAPILoader instance configured for URL fetching.
        """

        def _fetch_from_url() -> dict[str, Any]:
            logger.info("Loading OpenAPI specification from URL: %s", url)
            req_headers = {"User-Agent": "langchain-openapi"}
            if headers:
                req_headers.update(headers)

            try:
                with httpx.Client(timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=True) as client:
                    response = client.get(url, headers=req_headers)
                    response.raise_for_status()
                    content = response.text
            except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
                logger.error("Failed to fetch OpenAPI spec from URL '%s': %s", url, exc)
                raise SpecLoadError(
                    f"Failed to fetch specification from URL '{url}': {exc}"
                ) from exc

            return parse_json_or_yaml(content)

        return cls(load_fn=_fetch_from_url, source_info=f"URL '{url}'")

    @classmethod
    def from_file(cls, file_path: str | Path) -> "OpenAPILoader":
        """Create an OpenAPILoader for a local JSON or YAML file source.

        Args:
            file_path: Path to the local OpenAPI specification file.

        Returns:
            An OpenAPILoader instance configured for file loading.
        """
        path = Path(file_path)

        def _read_from_file() -> dict[str, Any]:
            logger.info("Loading OpenAPI specification from file: %s", path)
            if not path.exists():
                logger.error("Specification file does not exist: %s", path)
                raise SpecLoadError(f"Specification file not found: '{path}'")

            if not path.is_file():
                logger.error("Path is not a regular file: %s", path)
                raise SpecLoadError(f"Path is not a regular file: '{path}'")

            try:
                content = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            except OSError as exc:
                logger.error("Error reading specification file '%s': %s", path, exc)
                raise SpecLoadError(
                    f"Error reading specification file '{path}': {exc}"
                ) from exc

            return parse_json_or_yaml(content)

        return cls(load_fn=_read_from_file, source_info=f"file '{path}'")

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, spec_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> "OpenAPILoader":
        """Create an OpenAPILoader from an in-memory dictionary.

        Args:
            spec_dict: Raw Python dictionary containing the OpenAPI specification.

        Returns:
            An OpenAPILoader instance configured for dictionary loading.
        """

        def _get_from_dict() -> dict[str, Any]:
            logger.info("Loading OpenAPI specification from in-memory dictionary")
            return spec_dict

        return cls(load_fn=_get_from_dict, source_info="in-memory dictionary")

    def load(self) -> OpenAPISpec:
        """Load, validate, and normalize the OpenAPI specification.

        Returns:
            An OpenAPISpec instance containing the normalized specification data.

        Raises:
            SpecLoadError: If loading from source or parsing JSON/YAML fails.
            InvalidSpecError: If required fields ('openapi', 'paths') are missing.
            UnsupportedVersionError: If the OpenAPI version is unsupported.
        """
        raw_data = self._load_fn()
        validate_raw_spec(raw_data)
        spec = OpenAPISpec.from_dict(raw_data)

        logger.info(
            "Successfully loaded OpenAPI spec '%s' (OpenAPI version %s) from %s",
            spec.title,
            spec.version,
            self._source_info,
        )
        return spec

class MiddlewarePipeline:
    """Orchestrates sequential execution of a list of Middleware instances."""

    def __init__(self, middlewares: Sequence[Middleware] | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize MiddlewarePipeline.

        Args:
            middlewares: Sequence of Middleware objects to execute in order.
        """
        self.middlewares = list(middlewares) if middlewares else []

    async def execute(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        transport_call: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Execute the middleware chain leading to transport_call.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request instance.
            transport_call: Final network transmission function.

        Returns:
            Final httpx.Response instance.
        """
        index = 0

        async def call_next(req: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
            nonlocal index
            if index < len(self.middlewares):
                mw = self.middlewares[index]
                index += 1
                return await mw.dispatch(req, call_next)
            return await transport_call(req)

        return await call_next(request)

class RetryMiddleware(Middleware):
    """Middleware for retrying failed HTTP requests with configurable backoff."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        retries: int = 3,
        backoff: str = "exponential",
        backoff_factor: float = 0.5,
        retry_status_codes: Sequence[int] = (429, 500, 502, 503, 504),
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize RetryMiddleware.

        Args:
            retries: Maximum number of retry attempts (default 3).
            backoff: Strategy, 'exponential' or 'fixed' (default 'exponential').
            backoff_factor: Base multiplier in seconds for backoff (default 0.5s).
            retry_status_codes: HTTP status codes to trigger retries.
        """
        self.retries = retries
        self.backoff = backoff
        self.backoff_factor = backoff_factor
        self.retry_status_codes = set(retry_status_codes)

    async def dispatch(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        call_next: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Dispatch request with automatic retries on failures or status codes.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request instance.
            call_next: Callable to next middleware/transport.

        Returns:
            The final httpx.Response instance.
        """
        attempt = 0
        last_exception: Exception | None = None

        while attempt <= self.retries:
            try:
                response = await call_next(request)
                if (
                    response.status_code in self.retry_status_codes
                    and attempt < self.retries
                ):
                    attempt += 1
                    delay = self._calculate_delay(attempt)
                    logger.warning(
                        "Retrying %s (attempt %d/%d) after HTTP %d (delay %.2fs)",
                        request.url,
                        attempt,
                        self.retries,
                        response.status_code,
                        delay,
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                    continue
                return response
            except (httpx.TransportError, httpx.TimeoutException) as exc:
                last_exception = exc
                if attempt < self.retries:
                    attempt += 1
                    delay = self._calculate_delay(attempt)
                    logger.warning(
                        "Retrying %s (attempt %d/%d) after error: %s (delay %.2fs)",
                        request.url,
                        attempt,
                        self.retries,
                        exc,
                        delay,
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                    continue
                raise

        if last_exception:
            raise last_exception
        return response

    def _calculate_delay(self, attempt: int) -> float:
        if self.backoff == "fixed":
            return float(self.backoff_factor)
        return float(self.backoff_factor * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))

    def __init__(self, requests_per_second: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Initialize RateLimitMiddleware.

        Args:
            requests_per_second: Maximum allowed requests per second (default 5.0).
        """
        if requests_per_second <= 0:
            raise ValueError("requests_per_second must be greater than zero.")

        self.rate = float(requests_per_second)
        self.capacity = float(requests_per_second)
        self.tokens = float(requests_per_second)
        self.last_update = time.monotonic()
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def dispatch(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        call_next: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Throttle outgoing request according to token availability.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request instance.
            call_next: Callable to next middleware/transport.

        Returns:
            The httpx.Response instance.
        """
        await self._acquire_token()
        return await call_next(request)

    async def _acquire_token(self) -> None:
        async with self._lock:
            while True:
                now = time.monotonic()
                elapsed = now - self.last_update
                self.last_update = now

                # Refill tokens based on elapsed time
                self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + elapsed * self.rate)

                if self.tokens >= 1.0:
                    self.tokens -= 1.0
                    break

                # Calculate required sleep duration to get 1 full token
                needed_tokens = 1.0 - self.tokens
                wait_time = needed_tokens / self.rate
                await asyncio.sleep(wait_time)

class CacheMiddleware(Middleware):
    """Middleware for caching HTTP GET responses."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        ttl: float = 300.0,
        backend: CacheBackend | None = None,
        cache_authenticated: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize CacheMiddleware.

        Args:
            ttl: Cache Time-To-Live in seconds (default 300.0s).
            backend: Cache backend provider (default InMemoryCacheBackend).
            cache_authenticated: If False, skip caching auth requests (default False).
        """
        self.ttl = ttl
        self.backend = backend or InMemoryCacheBackend()
        self.cache_authenticated = cache_authenticated

    async def dispatch(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        call_next: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Cache HTTP GET requests based on method, URL, and headers.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request.
            call_next: Callable to next middleware/transport.

        Returns:
            The httpx.Response instance.
        """
        # 1. Only cache GET requests
        if request.method.upper() != "GET":
            return await call_next(request)

        # 2. Skip caching if request has auth headers and cache_authenticated is False
        if not self.cache_authenticated and self._is_authenticated(request):
            return await call_next(request)

        key = self._generate_cache_key(request)

        # 3. Check cache
        cached = await self.backend.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            logger.info("Cache hit for %s", request.url)
            return cached

        # 4. Fetch response and cache successful GET responses (status 200)
        logger.info("Cache miss for %s", request.url)
        response = await call_next(request)

        if response.status_code == 200:
            await self.backend.set(key, response, self.ttl)

        return response

    def _is_authenticated(self, request: httpx.Request) -> bool:
        auth_headers = {"authorization", "cookie", "x-api-key"}
        return any(h.lower() in auth_headers for h in request.headers)

    def _generate_cache_key(self, request: httpx.Request) -> str:
        key_raw = f"{request.method.upper()}:{request.url}"
        return hashlib.sha256(key_raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

class PaginationMiddleware(Middleware):
    """Middleware for automated multi-page result aggregation."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        max_pages: int = 10,
        max_items: int = 1000,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize PaginationMiddleware.

        Args:
            max_pages: Maximum number of pages to fetch (default 10).
            max_items: Maximum total items to aggregate (default 1000).
        """
        self.max_pages = max_pages
        self.max_items = max_items

    async def dispatch(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        call_next: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Dispatch request, performing pagination if requested.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request.
            call_next: Callable to next middleware/transport.

        Returns:
            Aggregated httpx.Response if pagination enabled, else single response.
        """
        params = dict(request.url.params)
        is_paginate_flag = (
            request.headers.get("X-LangChain-Paginate", "").lower() == "true"
            or params.pop("__paginate__", "").lower() == "true"
        )

        if not is_paginate_flag:
            return await call_next(request)

        # Remove header/param before sending to avoid server errors
        if "X-LangChain-Paginate" in request.headers:
            del request.headers["X-LangChain-Paginate"]
        request.url = request.url.copy_with(params=params)

        # Initial request
        response = await call_next(request)
        if response.status_code != 200:
            return response

        try:
            initial_data = json.loads(response.text)
        except Exception:
            return response

        aggregated_items, data_key = self._extract_items(initial_data)
        if aggregated_items is None:
            return response

        base_payload = initial_data
        current_page = 1
        page_param_name, _current_val = self._detect_pagination_param(params)

        while current_page < self.max_pages and len(aggregated_items) < self.max_items:
            current_page += 1
            next_params = dict(params)

            if page_param_name == "page":
                next_params["page"] = str(current_page)
            elif page_param_name == "offset":
                limit = int(params.get("limit", len(aggregated_items)))
                next_params["offset"] = str((current_page - 1) * limit)
            elif page_param_name == "cursor" and isinstance(initial_data, dict):
                cursor_val = initial_data.get("next_cursor") or initial_data.get(
                    "cursor"
                )
                if not cursor_val:
                    break
                next_params["cursor"] = str(cursor_val)
            else:
                next_params["page"] = str(current_page)

            next_req = httpx.Request(
                method=request.method,
                url=request.url.copy_with(params=next_params),
                headers=request.headers,
                content=request.content,
            )

            page_resp = await call_next(next_req)
            if page_resp.status_code != 200:
                break

            try:
                page_data = json.loads(page_resp.text)
            except Exception:
                break

            page_items, _ = self._extract_items(page_data)
            if not page_items:
                break

            aggregated_items.extend(page_items)
            initial_data = page_data

            if len(aggregated_items) >= self.max_items:
                aggregated_items = aggregated_items[: self.max_items]
                break

        # Re-encode aggregated response payload
        final_payload: Any
        if data_key is not None and isinstance(base_payload, dict):
            base_payload[data_key] = aggregated_items
            final_payload = base_payload
        else:
            final_payload = aggregated_items

        return httpx.Response(
            status_code=200,
            headers=response.headers,
            content=json.dumps(final_payload).encode("utf-8"),
            request=request,
        )

    def _extract_items(self, data: Any) -> tuple[list[Any] | None, str | None]:
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return list(data), None
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            for key in ("items", "data", "results", "records"):
                if key in data and isinstance(data[key], list):
                    return list(data[key]), key
        return None, None

    def _detect_pagination_param(self, params: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
        for p in ("page", "offset", "cursor"):
            if p in params:
                return p, params[p]
        return "page", "1"

class LoggingMiddleware(Middleware):
    """Middleware for logging HTTP request/response metrics."""

    def __init__(self, logger_instance: logging.Logger | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize LoggingMiddleware.

        Args:

        """
        self.logger = logger_instance or logger

    async def dispatch(
        self,
        request: httpx.Request,
        call_next: NextCallable,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Log outgoing request metrics and incoming response status.

        Args:
            request: Outgoing httpx.Request.
            call_next: Callable to next middleware/transport.

        Returns:
            The httpx.Response instance.
        """
        sanitized = sanitize_request_log(request.method, str(request.url))
        start_time = time.monotonic()
        self.logger.info("HTTP Request: %s", sanitized)

        try:
            response = await call_next(request)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
            self.logger.info(
                "HTTP Response: %s -> Status %d (%.3fs)",
                sanitized,
                response.status_code,
                elapsed,
            )
            return response
        except Exception as exc:
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
            self.logger.error(
                "HTTP Exception: %s failed after %.3fs: %s",
                sanitized,
                elapsed,
                exc,
            )
            raise

class OpenAPIParser:
    """Parser for converting an OpenAPISpec into normalized internal Python models.

    Limitations:
        Poly-schema keywords (oneOf, anyOf, allOf, discriminator), callbacks, links,
        webhooks, and advanced example inheritance are currently skipped.
    """

    def __init__(self, spec: OpenAPISpec) -> None:
        """Initialize parser with an OpenAPISpec instance.

        Args:
            spec: The normalized OpenAPI specification object.
        """
        self._spec = spec
        self._resolver = ReferenceResolver(spec.raw)

    def parse(self) -> list[Operation]:
        """Parse all paths and operations in the specification.

        Returns:
            A list of strongly typed Operation instances.
        """
        logger.info("Parsing OpenAPI operations for '%s'", self._spec.title)
        resolved_spec = self._resolver.resolve(self._spec.raw)
        global_security = resolved_spec.get("security", [])

        operations: list[Operation] = []
        paths: dict[str, Any] = resolved_spec.get("paths", {})

        for path, path_item in paths.items():
            if not isinstance(path_item, dict):
                continue

            path_params = self._parse_parameters(path_item.get("parameters", []))

            for key, val in path_item.items():
                if key.upper() not in HTTPMethod.__members__:
                    continue

                if not isinstance(val, dict):
                    continue

                method = HTTPMethod(key.upper())
                operation = self._parse_operation(
                    method=method,
                    path=path,
                    op_dict=val,
                    path_params=path_params,
                    global_security=global_security,
                )
                operations.append(operation)

        logger.info(
            "Parsed %d operations from OpenAPI spec '%s'",
            len(operations),
            self._spec.title,
        )
        return operations

    def _parse_operation(
        self,
        method: HTTPMethod,
        path: str,
        op_dict: dict[str, Any],
        path_params: list[Parameter],
        global_security: list[dict[str, list[str]]],
    ) -> Operation:
        explicit_id = op_dict.get("operationId")
        if explicit_id and isinstance(explicit_id, str):
            op_id: str | None = explicit_id
            name = explicit_id
        else:
            op_id = None
            name = generate_fallback_operation_name(method.value, path)

        summary = op_dict.get("summary")
        description = op_dict.get("description")
        deprecated = bool(op_dict.get("deprecated", False))
        tags = [str(t) for t in op_dict.get("tags", []) if isinstance(t, str)]

        # Combine parameters (operation-level overrides path-level)
        op_param_list = self._parse_parameters(op_dict.get("parameters", []))
        param_map: dict[tuple[str, str], Parameter] = {}
        for p in path_params:
            param_map[(p.name, p.location.value)] = p
        for p in op_param_list:
            param_map[(p.name, p.location.value)] = p

        parameters = list(param_map.values())

        # Parse requestBody
        request_body = self._parse_request_body(op_dict.get("requestBody"))

        # Parse responses
        responses = self._parse_responses(op_dict.get("responses"))

        # Security
        if "security" in op_dict:
            security = op_dict["security"]
        else:
            security = global_security

        return Operation(
            name=name,
            method=method,
            path=path,
            summary=str(summary) if summary is not None else None,
            description=str(description) if description is not None else None,
            operation_id=op_id,
            tags=tags,
            parameters=parameters,
            request_body=request_body,
            responses=responses,
            deprecated=deprecated,
            security=security if isinstance(security, list) else [],
        )

    def _parse_parameters(self, raw_params: list[Any]) -> list[Parameter]:
        params: list[Parameter] = []
        if not isinstance(raw_params, list):
            return params

        for item in raw_params:
            if not isinstance(item, dict):
                continue

            name = item.get("name")
            location_str = item.get("in")
            if not name or not location_str or not isinstance(name, str):
                continue

            try:
                location = ParameterLocation(location_str)
            except ValueError:
                logger.warning(
                    "Skipping parameter '%s' with unknown location '%s'",
                    name,
                    location_str,
                )
                continue

            is_path = location == ParameterLocation.PATH
            required = bool(item.get("required", True if is_path else False))
            description = item.get("description")
            schema_dict = item.get("schema")
            schema = self._parse_schema(schema_dict) if schema_dict else None

            default = item.get("default")
            if default is None and schema and schema.default is not None:
                default = schema.default

            example = item.get("example")
            style = item.get("style")
            explode = item.get("explode")

            params.append(
                Parameter(
                    name=name,
                    location=location,
                    required=required,
                    description=str(description) if description is not None else None,
                    schema=schema,
                    default=default,
                    example=example,
                    style=str(style) if style is not None else None,
                    explode=bool(explode) if explode is not None else None,
                )
            )

        return params

    def _parse_request_body(
        self, raw_body: dict[str, Any] | None
    ) -> RequestBody | None:
        if not isinstance(raw_body, dict):
            return None

        required = bool(raw_body.get("required", False))
        description = raw_body.get("description")
        content_dict = raw_body.get("content", {})
        content: dict[str, MediaType] = {}

        if isinstance(content_dict, dict):
            for content_type, media_raw in content_dict.items():
                if isinstance(media_raw, dict):
                    media_type = self._parse_media_type(str(content_type), media_raw)
                    content[str(content_type)] = media_type

        return RequestBody(
            required=required,
            description=str(description) if description is not None else None,
            content=content,
        )

    def _parse_responses(
        self, raw_responses: dict[str, Any] | None
    ) -> dict[str, Response]:
        responses: dict[str, Response] = {}
        if not isinstance(raw_responses, dict):
            return responses

        for status_code, resp_raw in raw_responses.items():
            if not isinstance(resp_raw, dict):
                continue

            desc = str(resp_raw.get("description", ""))
            content_dict = resp_raw.get("content", {})
            content: dict[str, MediaType] = {}

            if isinstance(content_dict, dict):
                for content_type, media_raw in content_dict.items():
                    if isinstance(media_raw, dict):
                        media_type = self._parse_media_type(
                            str(content_type), media_raw
                        )
                        content[str(content_type)] = media_type

            responses[str(status_code)] = Response(
                status_code=str(status_code),
                description=desc,
                content=content,
            )

        return responses

    def _parse_media_type(
        self, content_type: str, raw_media: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> MediaType:
        schema_dict = raw_media.get("schema")
        schema = (
            self._parse_schema(schema_dict) if isinstance(schema_dict, dict) else None
        )
        example = raw_media.get("example")
        examples = raw_media.get("examples")

        return MediaType(
            content_type=content_type,
            schema=schema,
            example=example,
            examples=examples if isinstance(examples, dict) else None,
        )

    def _parse_schema(self, raw_schema: dict[str, Any] | None) -> Schema | None:
        if not isinstance(raw_schema, dict):
            return None

        raw_type = raw_schema.get("type")
        nullable = bool(raw_schema.get("nullable", False))
        type_val: DataType | str | list[DataType | str] | None = None

        if isinstance(raw_type, str):
            try:
                type_val = DataType(raw_type)
            except ValueError:
                type_val = raw_type
        elif isinstance(raw_type, list):
            parsed_types: list[DataType | str] = []
            for t in raw_type:
                if t == "null":
                    nullable = True
                elif isinstance(t, str):
                    try:
                        parsed_types.append(DataType(t))
                    except ValueError:
                        parsed_types.append(t)
            type_val = parsed_types

        format_val = raw_schema.get("format")
        description = raw_schema.get("description")
        default = raw_schema.get("default")
        enum = raw_schema.get("enum")
        required_list = raw_schema.get("required")

        # Properties (object)
        props_dict = raw_schema.get("properties")
        properties: dict[str, Schema] | None = None
        if isinstance(props_dict, dict):
            properties = {}
            for p_name, p_schema in props_dict.items():
                if isinstance(p_schema, dict):
                    parsed_p = self._parse_schema(p_schema)
                    if parsed_p:
                        properties[str(p_name)] = parsed_p

        # Items (array)
        items_dict = raw_schema.get("items")
        items: Schema | None = None
        if isinstance(items_dict, dict):
            items = self._parse_schema(items_dict)

        return Schema(
            type=type_val,
            format=str(format_val) if format_val is not None else None,
            properties=properties,
            items=items,
            required=[str(r) for r in required_list]
            if isinstance(required_list, list)
            else None,
            enum=list(enum) if isinstance(enum, list) else None,
            default=default,
            nullable=nullable,
            description=str(description) if description is not None else None,
        )

def parse(self) -> list[Operation]:
    """Parse all paths and operations in the specification.

    Returns:
        A list of strongly typed Operation instances.
    """
    logger.info("Parsing OpenAPI operations for '%s'", self._spec.title)
    resolved_spec = self._resolver.resolve(self._spec.raw)
    global_security = resolved_spec.get("security", [])

    operations: list[Operation] = []
    paths: dict[str, Any] = resolved_spec.get("paths", {})

    for path, path_item in paths.items():
        if not isinstance(path_item, dict):
            continue

        path_params = self._parse_parameters(path_item.get("parameters", []))

        for key, val in path_item.items():
            if key.upper() not in HTTPMethod.__members__:
                continue

            if not isinstance(val, dict):
                continue

            method = HTTPMethod(key.upper())
            operation = self._parse_operation(
                method=method,
                path=path,
                op_dict=val,
                path_params=path_params,
                global_security=global_security,
            )
            operations.append(operation)

    logger.info(
        "Parsed %d operations from OpenAPI spec '%s'",
        len(operations),
        self._spec.title,
    )
    return operations

class ReferenceResolver:
    """Recursively resolves local JSON pointers (e.g. #/components/schemas/Pet).

    Limitations:
        Only local references starting with '#/' are currently supported.
        Remote pointers (URLs or relative files) will raise an InvalidSpecError.
    """

    def __init__(self, raw_spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Initialize resolver with the full raw OpenAPI specification dictionary.

        Args:
            raw_spec: The root OpenAPI specification dictionary.
        """
        self._raw_spec = raw_spec

    def resolve(self, data: Any, seen: set[str] | None = None) -> Any:
        """Recursively resolve $ref pointers within a data structure.

        Args:
            data: The dictionary, list, or scalar value containing potential $ref keys.
            seen: Set of already traversed $ref pointers to prevent infinite loops.

        Returns:
            The input data structure with all local $ref pointers replaced by targets.

        Raises:
            InvalidSpecError: If a $ref pointer is invalid or remote.
        """
        if seen is None:
            seen = set()

        if isinstance(data, dict):
            if "$ref" in data and isinstance(data["$ref"], str):
                ref_path = data["$ref"]
                if not ref_path.startswith("#/"):
                    raise InvalidSpecError(
                        f"Unsupported reference format '{ref_path}'. "
                        "Only local references starting with '#/' are supported."
                    )

                if ref_path in seen:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Circular reference detected for pointer '%s'", ref_path
                    )
                    shallow_copy = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != "$ref"}
                    return self.resolve(shallow_copy, seen=seen)

                seen_next = set(seen)
                seen_next.add(ref_path)

                resolved_target = self._lookup_pointer(ref_path)
                sibling_keys = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != "$ref"}

                if isinstance(resolved_target, dict):
                    merged = dict(resolved_target)
                    merged.update(sibling_keys)
                    return self.resolve(merged, seen=seen_next)

                return self.resolve(resolved_target, seen=seen_next)

            return {k: self.resolve(v, seen=seen) for k, v in data.items()}

        if isinstance(data, list):
            return [self.resolve(item, seen=seen) for item in data]

        return data

    def _lookup_pointer(self, ref_path: str) -> Any:
        """Navigate the raw spec using a local JSON pointer string.

        Args:
            ref_path: JSON pointer starting with '#/'.

        Returns:
            The resolved target object.

        Raises:
            InvalidSpecError: If the pointer path cannot be found in raw_spec.
        """
        parts = [
            p.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~") for p in ref_path[2:].split("/")
        ]
        curr: Any = self._raw_spec

        for part in parts:
            if isinstance(curr, dict) and part in curr:
                curr = curr[part]
            elif isinstance(curr, list) and part.isdigit() and int(part) < len(curr):
                curr = curr[int(part)]
            else:
                raise InvalidSpecError(
                    f"Failed to resolve reference '{ref_path}': key '{part}' not found."
                )

        return curr

class OpenAPIToolkit:
    """Toolkit for managing and filtering LangChain tools generated from OpenAPI specs.

    Attributes:
        spec: The parsed OpenAPISpec model.
        executor: AsyncHTTPExecutor instance.
        tools: List of generated LangChain tools.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        spec: OpenAPISpec,
        provider: RequestProvider | None = None,
        auth: AuthProvider | None = None,
        middleware: Sequence[Middleware] | None = None,
        timeout: float = 30.0,
        base_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize OpenAPIToolkit.

        Args:
            spec: Loaded OpenAPISpec.
            provider: Optional RequestProvider for HTTP request mutation.
            auth: Legacy AuthProvider for backwards compatibility.
            middleware: Sequence of Middleware instances for production resilience.
            timeout: Request execution timeout in seconds.
            base_url: Optional base URL overriding the specification servers list.
        """
        self.spec = spec

        # Determine effective base URL from override or first server entry
        effective_base_url = base_url
        if not effective_base_url and spec.servers:
            effective_base_url = spec.servers[0]

        self.executor = AsyncHTTPExecutor(
            base_url=effective_base_url,
            provider=provider,
            auth=auth,
            middleware=middleware,
            timeout=timeout,
        )
        self.factory = LangChainToolFactory(executor=self.executor)

        # Parse operations and create tools with unique names
        parser = OpenAPIParser(spec)
        operations = parser.parse()

        self._tools_dict: dict[str, BaseTool] = {}
        used_names: set[str] = set()

        for op in operations:
            base_name = format_tool_name(op)
            candidate_name = base_name
            counter = 2
            while candidate_name in used_names:
                candidate_name = f"{base_name}_{counter}"
                counter += 1

            used_names.add(candidate_name)
            tool = self.factory.create_tool(op, name_override=candidate_name)
            self._tools_dict[candidate_name] = tool

        logger.info(
            "OpenAPIToolkit initialized with %d tools.",
            len(self._tools_dict),
        )

            middleware: Sequence of Middleware instances.

            base_url: Optional base URL override for API execution.

            An initialized OpenAPIToolkit instance.

            spec=spec,
            provider=provider,
            auth=auth,
            middleware=middleware,
            timeout=timeout,
            base_url=base_url,
        )

    def list_tools(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return a list of all generated tool names in the toolkit.

        Returns:
            List of tool name strings.
        """
        return list(self._tools_dict.keys())

    def get_tool(self, name: str) -> BaseTool:
        """Get a specific tool by name.

        Args:
            name: The name of the tool to retrieve.

        Returns:
            The matching BaseTool instance.

        Raises:
            KeyError: If no tool with the given name exists in the toolkit.
        """
        if name not in self._tools_dict:
            available = self.list_tools()
            raise KeyError(
                f"Tool '{name}' not found in toolkit. Available tools: {available}"
            )
        return self._tools_dict[name]

    def get_tools(
        self,
        methods: list[str] | None = None,
        tags: list[str] | None = None,
        include: list[str] | None = None,
        exclude: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> list[BaseTool]:
        """Retrieve tools from the toolkit with optional filtering.

        Args:
            methods: Filter tools by HTTP method (e.g. ['GET', 'POST']).
            tags: Filter tools by OpenAPI tag (e.g. ['Pet', 'Store']).
            include: List of tool names or operation_ids to explicitly include.
            exclude: List of tool names or operation_ids to explicitly exclude.

        Returns:
            Filtered list of LangChain BaseTool instances.
        """
        result: list[BaseTool] = []
        target_methods = [m.upper() for m in methods] if methods else None
        inc_set = set(include) if include else None
        exc_set = set(exclude) if exclude else None

        for tool_name, tool in self._tools_dict.items():
            meta = tool.metadata or {}
            op_id = meta.get("operation_id")
            method = meta.get("method")
            op_tags = meta.get("tags") or []

            # 1. Exclude filter
            if exc_set and (tool_name in exc_set or (op_id and op_id in exc_set)):
                continue

            # 2. Include filter
            if inc_set and not (tool_name in inc_set or (op_id and op_id in inc_set)):
                continue

            # 3. HTTP Methods filter
            if target_methods and method not in target_methods:
                continue

            # 4. Tags filter
            if tags and not any(t in op_tags for t in tags):
                continue

            result.append(tool)

        return result

def get_tool(self, name: str) -> BaseTool:
    """Get a specific tool by name.

    Args:
        name: The name of the tool to retrieve.

    Returns:
        The matching BaseTool instance.

    Raises:

    if name not in self._tools_dict:
        available = self.list_tools()
        raise KeyError(
            f"Tool '{name}' not found in toolkit. Available tools: {available}"
        )
    return self._tools_dict[name]

def get_tools(
    self,
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    include: list[str] | None = None,
    exclude: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[BaseTool]:
    """Retrieve tools from the toolkit with optional filtering.

    Args:
        methods: Filter tools by HTTP method (e.g. ['GET', 'POST']).
        tags: Filter tools by OpenAPI tag (e.g. ['Pet', 'Store']).
        include: List of tool names or operation_ids to explicitly include.
        exclude: List of tool names or operation_ids to explicitly exclude.

    Returns:
        Filtered list of LangChain BaseTool instances.
    """
    result: list[BaseTool] = []
    target_methods = [m.upper() for m in methods] if methods else None
    inc_set = set(include) if include else None
    exc_set = set(exclude) if exclude else None

    for tool_name, tool in self._tools_dict.items():
        meta = tool.metadata or {}
        op_id = meta.get("operation_id")
        method = meta.get("method")
        op_tags = meta.get("tags") or []

        # 1. Exclude filter
        if exc_set and (tool_name in exc_set or (op_id and op_id in exc_set)):
            continue

        # 2. Include filter
        if inc_set and not (tool_name in inc_set or (op_id and op_id in inc_set)):
            continue

        # 3. HTTP Methods filter
        if target_methods and method not in target_methods:
            continue

        # 4. Tags filter
        if tags and not any(t in op_tags for t in tags):
            continue

        result.append(tool)

    return result

class LangChainToolFactory:
    """Factory for creating LangChain StructuredTool instances from Operations."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        executor: AsyncHTTPExecutor | None = None,
        schema_converter: SchemaConverter | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize LangChainToolFactory.

        Args:
            executor: Optional AsyncHTTPExecutor instance for execution.
            schema_converter: Optional SchemaConverter instance.
        """
        self.executor = executor or AsyncHTTPExecutor()
        self.schema_converter = schema_converter or SchemaConverter()

    def create_tool(
        self,
        operation: Operation,
        name_override: str | None = None,
    ) -> StructuredTool:
        """Convert an Operation model into a fully functional LangChain StructuredTool.

        Args:
            operation: The Operation model to convert.
            name_override: Optional name overriding the generated tool name.

        Returns:
            A LangChain StructuredTool instance.
        """
        tool_name = name_override or format_tool_name(operation)
        description_text = build_tool_description(operation)
        args_schema = self.schema_converter.to_pydantic(operation)
        executor = self.executor

        async def _arun(**kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            try:
                result = await executor.execute(operation, kwargs)
                if result.status_code >= 400:
                    raise ToolException(
                        f"HTTP request failed with status code "
                        f"{result.status_code}: {result.body}"
                    )
                return result.body
            except ToolException:
                raise
            except HTTPExecutionError as exc:
                raise ToolException(f"API execution error: {exc}") from exc
            except Exception as exc:
                raise ToolException(f"Tool execution error: {exc}") from exc

        def _run(**kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            try:
                loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
            except RuntimeError:
                loop = None

            if loop and loop.is_running():
                import concurrent.futures

                with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
                    future = pool.submit(lambda: asyncio.run(_arun(**kwargs)))
                    return future.result()
            else:
                return asyncio.run(_arun(**kwargs))

        metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
            "method": operation.method.value.upper(),
            "path": operation.path,
            "operation_id": operation.operation_id,
            "tags": operation.tags,
        }

        logger.debug(
            "Created StructuredTool '%s' for %s %s",
            tool_name,
            operation.method.value.upper(),
            operation.path,
        )

        return StructuredTool.from_function(
            func=_run,
            coroutine=_arun,
            name=tool_name,
            description=description_text,
            args_schema=args_schema,
            metadata=metadata,
            handle_tool_error=True,
        )

import asyncio
from langchain_openapi import OpenAPIToolkit, RetryMiddleware, LoggingMiddleware


async def main():
    # 1. Initialize toolkit with retries and logging
    toolkit = OpenAPIToolkit.from_url(
        "https://api.crossref.org/swagger-docs",
        middleware=[
            LoggingMiddleware(),
            RetryMiddleware(retries=3),
        ],
    )

    # 2. Get tools
    tools = toolkit.get_tools()
    print(f"Loaded {len(tools)} tools from Crossref OpenAPI spec.")

    # 3. Execute search tool
    search_tool = toolkit.get_tool("search_works")
    if search_tool:
        result = await search_tool.ainvoke({"query": "LangChain"})
        print("Search Results:", result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
